findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the handwashing sink next to the dry storage room does not have cold water; the handle fell off when turned. PIC was informed by staff that the Owner was aware of the situation and a replacement has been ordered, but the sink had not been removed from service to stop staff from using it. PIC removed the handwashing sink from service with signs, “No Usar/Out of Order”. Another handwashing sink is available for use by kitchen staff without having to leave the kitchen. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are equipped to provide hot water.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the available test strips for Chlorine were damaged by water from the chemical dish machine. Facility does have test strips for quaternary ammonium, but does not have replacement strips for Chlorine (bleach). Ensure that concentrations of all sanitizing solutions can be accurately determined by using a test kit.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the walls behind the dish line have an accumulation of soil residues. PIC was notified. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there is a buildup of debris on the ice machine baffles. The PIC was reminded that food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 10 April 2026 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the concentration of the sanitizer bucket (quat) in the right serving area was low (100ppm). The PIC was notified, and inspectors educated that the sanitizer solution (sourced from the triple sink) may need to run for additional time to reach the correct concentration. The PIC remade the sanitizer solution for the bucket and it tested at 200pm (quat). Sanitizing solution should be tested frequently to confirm it is at an effective sanitizing concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the caulking behind the chemical dishwasher area and the neighboring triple sink between the equipment and the wall was in disrepair. PIC was informed of the issue, and assured inspectors that the necessary repairs will be done by the next routine inspection. It is important that all food surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee turned off the faucets after hand washing with their bare hands. The employee was educated that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucets to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Educational hand washing handouts were provided and the inspector suggests posting above the hand sinks. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw meat stored on the shelf above onions in the walk-in cooler.

(2) Raw eggs stored on the shelf above various sauces in the double door cooler on the cookline. 

The storage order violations were correct during the inspection. Educational handouts were provided and the inspector suggests posting them in the kitchen. Ensure that raw meats and eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed a large amount of cooked beans cooling in a deep, covered container on the counter at room temperature. The PIC stated that the beans had been cooling for about an hour. The inspector probed the beans and the internal temperature was 105F. The PIC was reminded that the beans must get below 70F in two hours. The beans were immediately separated into multiple uncovered containers to allow air flow through more of the food and moved into the walk-in cooler. The PIC was educated about the importance of using proper cooling methods and educational handouts were provided. The inspector will follow-up on 11/7/2025 to check on cooling practices at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed raw fish that bears a label indicating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing inside of the packaging in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was educated and an employee removed the fish from the packaging during the inspection. Ensure that required foods are always removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the counter in the server area. The PIC was educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizing solutions between uses. The wiping cloth was removed for laundering during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always held in chemical sanitizer when not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sugar container in the dry storage area has a bowl for a scoop. All scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid contamination. Ensure that the sugar container has a scoop with a handle by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The accumulation of dust and other debris on the walk-in cooler fans. 

(2) The accumulation of food debris in the container holding clean utensils on the storage shelves by the dish machine. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw eggs stored over horchata (prepared ready-to-eat drink) and various sauces in the double door cooler. The PIC was educated and the eggs were moved onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw eggs are always stored below ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). Dishes and other equipment can still be washed and rinsed in the dish machine; however, they must be sanitized in the triple sink until the dish machine is properly sanitizing. During the inspection the triple sink was setup with sanitizer. The inspector will follow-up on 7/21/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed there is a buildup of debris on the ice machine baffles and the can opener blade. The PIC was reminded that food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 7/28/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles and can opener blade have been cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a jug of milk that was opened yesterday and a container of horchata (ready-to-eat milk based drink) that was prepared yesterday were not date marked. The PIC was educated and the milk and horchata were date marked during the inspection. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods held at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed various foods stored uncovered in the white reach-in freezer and uncovered taco shells on the cookline. The PIC was educated that all foods must be covered to avoid contamination. Ensure that foods are properly covered during storage by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed cooked rice and pico de gallo in the left prep cooler had bowls for scoops. All scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid contamination. During the inspection the PIC removed the bowls. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods have scoops with a handle that are stored properly by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bucket that holds the ice machine scoop has an accumulation of debris on the bottom. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Observed the following improper hand washing sink usage during the inspection:

(1) During the inspection an employee was observed washing the soda dispenser holder in the hand washing sink by the dish machine. When the action was observed the employee was educated that hand washing sinks cannot be used for any purpose other than hand washing.

(2) The inspector observed dumped ice in the bar hand washing sink. The PIC was reminded that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. The bar currently has two sinks designated as hand washing sinks directly across from each other. The inspector suggests designating only one as the hand sink and using the other as a dump sink to avoid improper use. The sink that will not be used for hand washing must have the ‘employees must wash hands before returning to work’ signage removed.

Ensure that hand washing sinks are never used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed caulking to the left of the dish washing machine is a dark black color and deteriorating. This portion of the dish washing area experiences a high level of moisture from the rinsing nozzle. The calking must be removed and replaced when it starts to show signs of deterioration from moisture. Ensure that the caulking is replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of ice inside the walk-in freezer underneath the fan and on the ceiling. The ice is also dripping onto the boxes of food underneath. The inspector suggests scheduling a defrost or contacting repair personal. Ensure that inside the walk-in freezer is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the ice scoop holder at the right service station had an accumulation of soil residues. The ice scoop holder was removed and washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the large container of salsa in the ice bath was not covered. Foods must be covered at all times to protect against potential falling debris and other contamination. The container of salsa was covered during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the baffles of the ice machine were soiled. An employee cleaned the baffles during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed the back door in the dry-storage area does not have a self-closer. Ensure there is a self-closer on the door to protect against the entry of insects and rodents by the next routine inspection. 

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed the soda gun holder at the bar was soiled with debris. The holder was removed from service and cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the floor drain below the left service area had an accumulation of black soil residue around it. The floor drain was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed a cell phone was stored on a clean wiping cloth. The phone was removed from this location and the wiping cloth was laundered. The inspector educated about proper personal item storage. Ensure that phones are stored away from food preparation areas to protect food and food contact surfaces from contamination. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Observed the wrong chemical was hooked up to the dispenser at the mop sink, and nobody was aware it was the incorrect chemical. There was a degreaser hooked up when it should have been a sanitizer. Due to this, multiple sanitizer buckets did not have functional amounts of sanitizer in them. Other buckets created separately with bleach did have the correct amount of sanitizer. Educated about hooking up the correct chemicals. The sanitizer buckets with incorrect concentrations were corrected on site.

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a CFM when the inspectors showed up at the facility. Ensure there is always at least one CFM on site during all hours of operation. An individual with a CFM arrived at the facility during the inspection.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there were not employee reporting forms at the facility. Ensure that there are signed forms stating employees must report health and activities related to disease to the PIC. Employee reporting agreements were supplied during the inspection and all employees signed the forms. Ensure they are kept in a safe space and readily available for inspectors at future inspections.

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion
findings.comment:
Observed there was not exclusion and restriction paperwork at the facility. Ensure there is paperwork which states that the PIC will exclude or restrict food employees from the food establishment in accordance with law. The exclusion and restriction paperwork was given to the PIC during the inspection. Ensure they are kept in a safe place and are readily available to show inspectors at future inspections. 

2-201.12: The PERSON IN CHARGE shall EXCLUDE or RESTRICT a FOOD EMPLOYEE from a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in accordance with Law  symptoms/diagnosis

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Observed that there was no written procedures for employees to respond to vomit or diarrheal events at the facility. The PIC was given a vomit or diarrheal event response sheet. Ensure they are kept in a safe place and readily available to show inspectors at future inspections.

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed that the ice machine at the bar had the ice scoop being stored with the handle in the ice. The PIC was educated and the handle was moved out of the ice. Ensure that the handle is stored out of the ice to prevent bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods.

3-301.11: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands except washing fruits and veggies (P).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed that the hand-washing sink at the bar did not have paper towels. The PIC moved paper towels to the hand-washing sink during the inspection. Ensure there are always paper towels at all hand-washing skinks at the facility.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed that the hand-washing sink at the bar did not have soap. The PIC moved hand soap to the hand-washing sink during the inspection. Ensure that there is always soap at all hand-washing sinks at the facility. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed that the hand-washing sink at the bar did not have a sign that notified food employees to wash their hands before returning to work. Signs that notify food employees to wash their hands before returning to work was provided to the PIC. Ensure that all hand-washing sinks in the facility have signs that notify employees to wash their hands before returning to work.

6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed that raw fish was stored below raw chicken in the walk in cooler. Inspectors educated about food being stored according to their proper storage order. During the inspection the raw fish was moved above the raw chicken. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
During the inspection the following food-contact surfaces were observed to not be cleaned to slight and touch: (1) Knife over the prep table; (2) Stickers on pans; (3) Soil on pan; (4) The holder for the soda nozzle at the bar; (5) Soil at the bottom of the cup holding utensils at the bar. The listed food-contact surfaces were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that all food contact surfaces remain clean to slight and touch

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed that there were chicken nuggets that were 55F (probed) in a prep-cooler. These chicken nuggets were thrown away during the inspection. Ensure that Temperature Control Foods (TCS) are maintained at 41F or less.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed that there was (1) Cottage cheese that had exceeded the manufacturers use-by date; (2) Meat being stored past the maximum 7-days allowed to store TCS foods. The cottage cheese exceeding the manufactures use-by-date and the meat being stored past the 7-day mark were both thrown out during the inspection by the PIC. Ensure that proper date marking procedures are followed.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed that there was not date-marking on four pans of queso which required dates. They were made in the establishment over at least 24 hours ago. TSC food being held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours requires a date and can be held for 7 days. Dates were added to the appropriate foods. Ensure that all foods which require date marking are labeled with the proper dates. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed that there was steak thawing sitting out at room temperature. The temperatures of the meat was 64F (probed). The meat was voluntarily throw away. The PIC was educated about the proper techniques of thawing. Ensure that food is thawed according to an approved method. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Observed that some coolers were missing hanging thermometers. Ensure that all coolers have thermometers to measure air temperatures. The PIC put thermometers in the coolers during the inspection. 

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed that the back door in the dry-storage area did not have a self-closer. Ensure that there is a self-closer on the door to protect against the entry of insects and rodents.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed there was a mop stored incorrectly with the head sitting in the bottom of the mop sink. The PIC was educated and stored the mop correctly during the inspection. Ensure that the mop head is always hanging in a manner that allows it to dry. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that there was accumulated pooling water under the coffee/soda areas that was developing a slimy substance indicating it was not being cleaned as frequently as needed. The PIC was educated and mopped the needed areas. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed there were several personal employee items (including food, phone charges, and clothing) mixed with the food and food products intended for customer consumption. The PIC was educated and they moved all the personal employee items onto a specific employee designated shelf that is away from food and food products intended for consumer consumption. Ensure that all employee personal items are kept separate from food and food products intended for consumer consumption.

6-305.11: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12:  There was not a certified food manager present during the inspection. See that more certified staff are present so that the facility always has a certified manager present.
(A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: A single container of cheese sauce on the steam table was observed (probed) at 119F. Food was just added to steam table after lunch. Cheese pan was pulled from steam table and returned to stove top to be reheated to 165F. Product was returned to steam table after being properly reheated. 

(A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above.
